procedural_matters: Based on SI 15.6, boats intending to request a hearing or request redress for an incident in the racing area shall radio their intention to the Race Committee, which SWE 800 did promptly.
SI 15.3 changes Rule 44.1 so that the Two-Turns Penalty is replaced by the One-Turn Penalty. 3 NED 393 took a one turn penalty after the incident 4 Jan Secher attended as an observer.
facts: race 3 on leg 4: Swe 800 fetching the windward mark 1 on the starboard layline.

conclusions: NED 393 on port failed to keep clear of SWE 800 on starboard, and broke RRS 10. It was reasonably possible for NED 393, keep clear boat, to avoid contact with SWE 800, right-of-way boat. NED 393 broke RRS 14. It was not reasonably possible for SWE 800, the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with NED 393 when it was clear that NED 393 was not keeping clear. SWE 800 did not break RRS 14. As the damage to SWE was serious (see WS Case 141), a One-Turn penalty was not an applicable penalty under RRS 44.1 (b).
